history.subject: Design: the Wave-4 datum design pass — the cech-port trigger DECISION, with the reasoning. The universal twist normalizes: the pinned twist is the pullback of O(n) along the landed finite map to ℙ¹ = divisorClass of n·(fiber), two-cover-trivial BY CONSTRUCTION (V₀⊓V₁ is the basic open of the pulled-back chart coordinate, so tⁿ is the unit cocycle) — this replaces the point-twist and kills its chart-ideal obstruction. But the universal CLASS does not normalize: two-cover-triviality on the pinned cover is an invariant obstruction (the image in Pic(V₀)×Pic(V₁), unchanged by twisting or moving divisors), and the datum's surjectivity leg must push forward arbitrary functor-point classes over arbitrary étale-affine tests — every dodge circles back to H⁰-base-change of an arbitrary class. Degree lane, the meromorphic bridge W1–W4 COMPLETE (Fable-authored): every Čech Picard class of the integral curve is a divisor class, and equal divisor classes differ by a principal divisor. W1 — sections embed in the function field by germ-at-η (injective on units), and every class L has a meromorphic presentation: elements f_x := germ_η of the cocycle pair values at the canonical base index η, with f_x/f_y = the cocycle on the nose in K(X)ˣ. W2 — the divisor of a presentation, D_x := ord_x(f_x), piece-independent (unit sections have trivial order) with finite support (per-piece principal-divisor finiteness + a finite subcover). W3, the heart — equal presentation divisors give equal classes: on a common refinement the element ratios have matching orders everywhere, the ord-matching lemma turns them into unit sections (via the D=0 divisor sheaf both ways), and the coboundary is checked INSIDE K(X)ˣ by germ injectivity — no sheaf gluing anywhere, per the worksheet's D1 invariant. W4 — extraction: equal classes give cobounding units gluing to one element g of K(X)ˣ with D − D' = div(g); full kernel description picClass_eq_iff. Endpoints: realization of every divisor, the anchored total class map CurveDivisor.picClass with additivity, picClass(div g) = 1, surjectivity (S) and extraction (X) — the degree map's substrate. AUDIT FINDING against deg-D1: the landed pointDivisor seals its equation behind a private postcondition too weak to pin the divisor (s = 1 satisfies it), so the intended statements are formally unprovable against it — the point construction is rebuilt here with the specification public (PointUniformizerData tracking germ_η s = uniformizer), and the one-patch repair recipe to collapse divisorClass into the anchored map is recorded. Degree lane, W5: the degree homomorphism on the Čech Picard group and the E-i..E-iii interface. classDeg : Additive Pic(X) →+ ℤ — the degree of any divisor presenting the class, well-defined because equal classes differ by a principal divisor (extraction) and principal divisors have degree zero (the χ-ledger), total by surjectivity; carrier chosen so values are honest integers with the hom laws free (an AddMonoidHom out of the additivized Picard group rather than Multiplicative-ℤ wrappers). E-i: classDeg [𝒪(D)] = deg D for every Weil divisor. E-ii: classDeg (L·L') = classDeg L + classDeg L'. E-iii: χ(𝒪(D)) = χ(𝒪) + classDeg [𝒪(D)], with the finiteness-free class-invariance χ(𝒪(D)) = χ(𝒪(D')) whenever [𝒪(D)] = [𝒪(D')] (extraction + the multiplication isomorphism + χ-transport — no choice anywhere). Curve form: χ(𝒪(D)) = 1 − genus C + classDeg [𝒪(D)] on the challenge curve, side-condition-free. The two structure-sheaf finiteness hypotheses ride exactly where the ledger needs them; the pushforward-rank reading of E-i deferred as its own statement.
